IS : 9662 ( Part I ) - 1980

Indian Standard
CODE OF PRACTICE FOR CONSTRUCTION AND ASSEMBLY OF LEATHER SEALING CUPS
PART I `U' CUPS

0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian
Institution Sectional Council. Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Standards on 31 December 1980, after the draft finalized by the Leather Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division

0.2 The leather sealing, cups ,are used as gland packing for pneumatic Sealing cups may be of different shapes and hydraulic system presses. and designs depending on the particular use, namely `U' cups, `U' cups ( Doubled ), `M' cups, `K' cups, etc. 0.3 The sealing cups are made from either full chrome tanned leather or combination tanned leather. The various requirements for leather of The cups are cut such types. have been given in IS : 3020-1976*. according to the shape and design from the type of leather selected. 0.4 At the instance of the Heavy Engineering Corporation Ltd, Ranchi, that such an item of acceptable quality was not available in our country, the Committee considered their request for formulating such codes of practice for construction and assembly of leather sealing cups for various' It is also types of cups so as to promote these production indiginously. felt that small and cottage scale producers are likely to take up the manufacturing of these cups. The material requirements, shape and dimensions have been covered in IS : 8863 ( Part I )-I9787 which is a necessary ad.junct to this standard. 0.5 In formulating this standard, assistance has been derived from the Czechoslovakian standard CSN 02 90 12- 1961 Leather-sealing-cups, directive for construction and assembly. *Specification for leather for oil seals (first reoision).
tSpecification for leather sealing cups: Part I `U' cups.

IS:9662(PartI)-1980 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part I ) lays down directions for construction and assembly of leather sealing cups, `U' cups.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 1640-

1960* shall apply.

3. CONSTRUCTION
3.1 Directions

AND

ASSEMBLY

for Construction

of sealing areas given in IS : 9664-1981t.

3.1.1 The area for sealing cups should be chosen as per the diameter

3.1.2 Construction of sealing area should be chosen in such a way that during assembly sealing should not get altered beyond the sharp edges of threads. 3.1.3 Wearing surface for sealing should be plating of the frictional surfaces is recommended precision of the sealing is desired. smooth. Chromium only in cases where

cup

3.1.4 Care should be taken to ensure accuracy of concentricity as the has to serve only as a sealing and not as a guiding element.

3.13 In order to increase the life of the cup in places where the cup has to operate in water, frictional areas should be lubricated with It should be ensured that emulsive emulsive grease during operation. grease could easily reach below the functional part of the cups. 3.1.6 Example of appropriate constructional setting- is illustrated in Fig. 1 in the case of `U' cups. Dimensions for cross sections are given in IS : 9664- 1981 t. 3.2 Directions
for Assembly

3.2.1 The functional surfaces shall be cleaned carefully without damaging them and by a mild coat of mineral oil ( pctrokum jelly ).

3.2.2 The frictional surfaces of cups are examined to avoid scratches or similar defects and the cut off wall of the cups shall be examined to avoid defects like longitudinal cracks, wrinkle, cuts, etc, which are likely to impair the function of the CUPS.

IS : 9662 ( Part I ) - 19S6 3.2.3 During assembly of sets of top cups, the cups are inserted into the packing space one by one in such a manner that, after assembly, the complete assembly should not get crossed. Leather cuttings should be inserted between top cups as filler. 3.2.4 Sharp metallic tool should not be used as assembly aid. 3.2.5 Packing cover should be tightened by means of separate opposite screws, symmetrical to the whole circumference. 3.26 After tightening, the cups should be only lightly clamped together between the housing rings and thrust rings, as excessive tightening may result in damage to the cups. 3.2.7 It is recommended that the cups should be softened before assembly. They should be soaked in molten tallow at about 50�C in case After taking the cup out of the storage for a long period is required. bath, softening of the hard places should be done by slight kneeding. 3.2.8 In hydraulic f water ) equipment, due to use for a long time, it will be necessary to drain the water from the sealing areas, clean the areas and the piston and preserve them by smearing grease. It is absolutely essential to lubricate the cups and protect them against desiccation or deformity.
